activities.anchor: Helium was found in the Sun's spectrum
activities.caption: call the gap — found in the sky before the lab
activities.name: qcHeliumEstimate

config.prompt: Helium was found in the Sun's spectrum in 1868. How many years passed before it was isolated on Earth?
config.why: 27 years — each element's quantised electron levels are a fingerprint, so astronomers read the composition of stars they will never touch.
config.context: Sodium's twin yellow lines identify it at parts-per-billion in streetlight spectra.

activities.anchor: the filling order (aufbau) then builds the table automatically
activities.caption: stack the chain from wave equation to table
activities.name: qcChainOrder

config.prompt: The logical chain behind the periodic table — put it in order:
items: Solve the Schrödinger equation for electrons around a nucleus
The standing-wave solutions are the orbitals
Each electron gets four quantum numbers — n, ℓ, mℓ, ms
Pauli: no two electrons share all four — every orbital caps at two
The aufbau filling order builds the periodic table automatically
config.why: Shell capacities 2, 8, 18 emerge from 2n² — Mendeleev organised by observation; Schrödinger explained the organisation.

activities.caption: true or false — orbitals on trial
activities.name: qcOrbitalJudge

statements.s: An orbital is a standing wave — a three-dimensional probability map where a measurement is likely to find the electron.
statements.why: The Bohr planet-orbit picture was scaffolding, demolished by de Broglie's matter waves and Heisenberg's uncertainty.

statements.s: Asking which path the electron took is physically meaningless.
statements.why: There is no trajectory — everything on this page inherits that correction.

statements.s: The s orbital is a sphere of likelihood and the p orbitals are two lobes.
statements.why: Shapes of probability: s spheres, p dumbbells, d cloverleaves.

statements.s: Orbitals are racetracks the electron laps at a fixed speed.
statements.why: No paths exist — only probability distributions.

activities.anchor: expose the split between chemistry and nuclear physics
activities.caption: file each fact — electron count or nucleus
activities.name: qcIsotopeBuckets

config.prompt: Chemistry is set by Z; the nucleus holds the rest. File each fact:

items.label: carbon-12 and carbon-14 react almost identically
chlorine's relative atomic mass 35.5 — a weighted average of two isotopes

config.why: Mass does matter, a little, through quantum zero-point motion — heavy water boils at 101.4 °C, not 100.0 °C.

activities.anchor: the ledger is the Born–Haber cycle
activities.caption: one line of the Born–Haber ledger is wrong
activities.name: qcLedgerSpot

config.prompt: One line of this Born–Haber ledger for NaCl is wrong. Find it.
lines: Vaporise sodium: +108 kJ/mol; half-dissociate chlorine: +122 kJ/mol
Ionise sodium: +496 kJ/mol; attach the electron to chlorine: −349 kJ/mol
Sum so far: +377 kJ/mol — strongly unfavourable
Assembling the crystal releases about −787 kJ/mol of lattice enthalpy
Electron transfer is driven by shells 'wanting' to be full
Total ΔH of formation ≈ −411 kJ/mol — favourable by a wide margin
config.correction: Electron transfer is driven by electrostatic bookkeeping — the lattice enthalpy pays for the ionisation, not any shell's desire.
config.why: Atoms have no wants: the Coulomb attraction summed over billions of ion pairs is what closes the ledger — and the same arithmetic explains MgCl₂'s formula and NaCl's 801 °C melting point.

activities.caption: pair each hybrid with its geometry
activities.name: qcHybridMatch

config.prompt: Hybridisation sets geometry — pair each with its example:

pairs.right: flat ethene with its exposed π bond — the site of all addition chemistry

config.why: Bond order — bonding minus antibonding electrons, divided by two — predicts stability, and explains why O₂ is paramagnetic where Lewis structures cannot.

activities.caption: call the magnitude — diamond's exit temperature
activities.name: qcDiamondEstimate

config.prompt: Diamond is a tetrahedral sp³ network with no plane of weakness. Roughly what temperature does it sublime at?
config.why: Near 3,600 °C — and it conducts heat several times better than copper (stiff-bond lattice vibrations) while remaining an electrical insulator.
config.context: Graphite: the same atoms, sp² sheets — a lubricant, an electrode, and Scotch-tape-peelable into graphene (2004, Nobel 2010).

activities.anchor: formalised in quantum physics as a
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the electron sea
activities.name: qcSeaCloze

config.text: Metals are the case covalent theory handles by giving up: the electrons delocalise over the whole crystal — the 'sea of electrons', formalised as a %%0%%. Malleability follows: the bonding is non-directional, so planes of atoms slip without breaking the glue — the reason salt crystals %%1%% and copper sheets %%2%%.
config.hint: One term names the filled band of levels; two verbs contrast the brittle lattice with the bending metal.
